knowledge:
- key_parameters: a=The shape parameter of the Poisson-Tweedie distribution (e.g., a=0 for negative binomial, a=1 for Poisson) used in testShapePT and gofTest ;; group=A vector indicating the experimental group/condition for each sample in tweeDE ;; mc.cores=Number of cores to use for parallel processing in tweeDE and tweeDEglm ;; log2fc=Minimum absolute log2 fold-change threshold used to filter results in print.tweeDE ;; pval.adjust=Maximum adjusted P-value threshold used to filter results in print.tweeDE ;; offset=Matrix of normalizing offsets (e.g., from cqn package) to incorporate into tweeDEglm or glmPT
- alternatives: edgeR=Mentioned as the underlying engine for normalizeCounts (which calls TMM and equalizeLibSizes). Users should use edgeR directly if they need more control over the normalization step ;; cqn=Mentioned for conditional quantile normalization to remove GC content or gene length biases, returning offsets that can be passed to tweeDEglm or glmPT
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing RNA-seq count data (or other count data) with a wide dynamic range and heavy tails (overdispersion) that do not fit standard Poisson or negative binomial distributions well.
- pitfalls: Assuming a negative binomial distribution is always adequate, as many genes show substantial discrepancy and heavy tails that require the more flexible Poisson-Tweedie distribution ;; Running gofTest on the entire genome can take a very long time; it is recommended to run it on a subset of genes first.

workflows.name: standard_differential_expression
workflows.intent: Perform differential expression analysis between two groups using the score-based tweeDE test.
input: genderNigerian (vector of group labels for each sample)
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize raw counts using normalizeCounts ;; 2. Filter out low-expression genes using filterCounts ;; 3. Test for differential expression using tweeDE ;; 4. Extract and annotate differentially expressed genes using print and merge ;; 5. Visualize results using MAplot and Vplot
workflows.code:
countsNigerianNorm <- normalizeCounts(countsNigerian, genderNigerian)
countsNigerianNorm <- filterCounts(countsNigerianNorm)
resPT <- tweeDE(countsNigerianNorm[geneSubset, ], group = genderNigerian)
print(resPT)
deGenes <- print(resPT, n=Inf, log2fc=log2(1.5), pval.adjust=0.05, print=FALSE)
deGenes <- merge(deGenes, annotEnsembl63, by="row.names", sort=FALSE)
deGenes <- rownames(print(resPT, n=Inf, log2fc=log2(1.5), pval.adjust=0.05, print=FALSE))
MAplot(resPT, cex=0.7, log2fc.cutoff=log2(1.5), highlight=hl, main="MA-plot")
Vplot(resPT, cex=0.7, highlight=hl, log2fc.cutoff=log2(1.5), pval.adjust.cutoff=0.05, main="Volcano plot")

workflows.name: generalized_linear_modeling
workflows.intent: Fit generalized linear models using the Poisson-Tweedie distribution to test for differential expression with covariates or offsets.
workflows.stages: 1. Fit a GLM for a single gene using glmPT ;; 2. Summarize and test the model using summary and anova ;; 3. Fit GLMs for multiple genes simultaneously using tweeDEglm ;; 4. (Optional) Incorporate CQN offsets into the GLM using the offset argument in tweeDEglm
workflows.code:
mod <- glmPT(countsNigerianNorm["ENSG00000070031",] ~ genderNigerian)
summary(mod)
anova(mod)
resPTglm <- tweeDEglm( ~ genderNigerian, counts = countsNigerianNorm[geneSubset,])
head(resPTglm[sort(resPTglm$pval.adjust, index.return = TRUE)$ix,])
tweeDEglm(~ genderNigerian, counts = countsNigerianNorm[geneSubset,], offset = cqn.subset$offset)

workflows.name: goodness_of_fit_testing
workflows.intent: Assess whether count data for genes fits a specific distribution (like negative binomial).
workflows.stages: 1. Perform goodness-of-fit testing across genes using gofTest ;; 2. Visualize the fit using quantile-quantile plots with qqchisq ;; 3. Compare empirical distributions against Poisson, negative binomial, and Poisson-Tweedie using compareCountDist
workflows.code:
chi2gof <- gofTest(countsNigerianNorm[geneSubset, ], a=0)
qq <- qqchisq(chi2gof, main="Chi2 Q-Q Plot", ylim = c(0, 60))
qq <- qqchisq(chi2gof, normal=TRUE, ylim = c(-5, 7))
